title: NPS & Alternatives: Boosting Returns with AIFs, REITs, InvITs
description: The National Pension System (NPS) is exploring increased allocation to alternative investments like AIFs, REITs, and InvITs. These instruments offer a pathway.

faq.q: What are AIFs, REITs, and InvITs?
faq.a: AIFs (Alternative Investment Funds) are privately pooled funds investing in diverse assets like private equity or venture capital. REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts) allow investment in income-generating real estate. InvITs (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) enable investment in infrastructure projects like roads and power lines.

faq.q: Are these investments currently available in NPS?
faq.a: Yes, NPS currently allows a limited allocation (up to 5% for 'Active Choice' subscribers) to 'Alternative Assets' under Asset Class A. The ongoing discussion is about potentially increasing this limit.

faq.q: What are the risks involved with these alternative investments?
faq.a: Key risks include illiquidity (difficulty in quickly selling units), market volatility specific to real estate or infrastructure sectors, and complexities in valuation compared to publicly traded assets.

faq.q: How do these differ from traditional mutual funds?
faq.a: While both are pooled investment vehicles, AIFs typically invest in less traditional, often private assets and cater to sophisticated investors. REITs and InvITs specifically focus on real estate and infrastructure assets, respectively, and are structured to distribute income regularly.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in these through NPS?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are eligible to subscribe to NPS, subject to PFRDA regulations. Any investment options available to resident Indians in NPS would generally also be available to NRIs.

faq.q: What is the maximum allocation to Alternative Assets in NPS?
faq.a: Currently, for subscribers opting for 'Active Choice', the maximum allocation permitted to 'Alternative Assets' (Scheme A) is 5% of the total NPS corpus.
